column4: Grok Session Exchanges are documented in `document/log/grok/` folder spreadsheets. Each exchange is documented within a session log; other session exchanges may be stored in other spreadsheets. The format and structure of these files may change thorughout project development. Each session exchange should begin with a titular name that can be used to reference the output link. Markdown output must be formatted so that it is easy to review and copy/paste within the session exchange. Serialized table data must have an ID column. Javascript code must follow style rules of omitting semi-colons from end of lines/statements; prefixing single `$` character to function definition paranthetical closures; outputting valid ES; importing paths based on examples from demonstrament and development folders; and limiting code comments throughout.

Review the Recourse library located at https://github.com/thomaspatrickwelborn/recourse/tree/refinement. The `refinement` branch is derived from the `main` branch and intended for different types of refinement. Review the `README.md` and `document` foldersystem for details about Recourse utility and interface. Review the `/demonstrament` folder for details about Recourse tests and Recourse validation. Review the `/development` folder for details about Recourse development. Notice that `pm2` is used to invoke different applications of development and demonstrament using Digital Flux Capacitor.

Recourse is an original coutility authored by myself. Recourse is a dependency of my other libraries including Core-Plex (https://github.com/thomaspatrickwelborn/core-plex), Objecture (https://github.com/thomaspatrickwelborn/objecture), Document Process Manager (https://github.com/thomaspatrickwelborn/document-process-manager),
Over time there will updates to migrate property event logic from Objecture to Recourse, but it is not necessarily the current focus of this session.
